turns.t: Morning. Sorry if I'm dripping on your floor, the rain is ridiculous out there, and the car park by the surgery is a joke. Twenty minutes I circled.
Don't worry about the floor. It's been awful all week, hasn't it? Come and sit down. I'm glad you made it in, Mr. Farrukh.
Right, well, I've got a meeting at half eleven, so can we be quick? My wife made me come. She said I'd be daft not to.
Then your wife is a sensible woman. Tell me what happened this morning, in your own words.
I was in the kitchen having my tea and I tried to say something to her and the words came out slurred. Like I'd had a few pints. It lasted about five minutes and then it was gone, just like that.
So your speech was slurred for about five minutes this morning, and it's back to normal now. Is that right?
Yes. Quite normal. I don't see what the fuss is about, honestly.
I'd rather make a fuss about it than ignore it. Did anything else happen at the same time? Anything odd in your arms, or your face?
There was a bit of tingling in my right hand. Pins and needles, as the wife says. That was gone at the same time.
Pins and needles in your right hand, and it settled with the speech. Anything else, like a headache, or feeling dizzy?
I did feel dizzy for a minute, when I stood up from the table, and then it was gone. But I'd been up since five, so it's probably that.
Perhaps. Now, I'll ask a few things that might sound blunt. Did your face droop, or any weakness in an arm or leg?
No, no weakness. My wife says my face looked normal, she'd have said otherwise, believe me.
Good. And any trouble with your vision, double vision, or part of it going dark?
No, nothing like that. My eyes were fine.
Okay. Any chest pain or a racing heartbeat this morning, or lately?
No, nothing wrong with my chest. I walk the dog every day and I'm fine.
And your breathing, any trouble there?
No. Is this going to take long? I've still got to find somewhere to park for the other thing.
Nearly done. I do need to ask about your past health. Any long-term conditions?
High blood pressure, the doctor told me a few years ago. And I'm borderline diabetic, they said, but I manage it with my diet.
So high blood pressure, and diabetes managed with diet. Do you smoke?
Ten a day, give or take. I know, I know, don't start.
I won't lecture you today. Are you allergic to anything that I should write down?
Latex. Rubber gloves give me a horrible rash on my hands. Hospitals always put a sticker on my notes about it.
Latex and a rash from gloves, noted. I'll tell the nurse to use non-latex ones. Let me do your readings now. Blood pressure is 158 over 94.
Pulse is 88, temperature 36.8, oxygen saturation 97 percent, and your breathing is 16 a minute.
Is that bad? It's always up when I come to a doctor.
It's a bit high, I'd like to see it come down, but it doesn't change what I need to do. Look at my nose, please, and follow my finger with your eyes.
Your face moves evenly on both sides, and your speech is perfectly clear now. Squeeze my fingers as hard as you can.
Like this? I'm quite strong, you know.
Yes, both hands are equally strong. That's reassuring. So, I know you're in a hurry, but I want to arrange a CT scan of your head today, at the hospital.
Today? I can't do today. I've got my meeting.
I understand, but what happened this morning needs to be looked at properly and soon. I also want an ECG done here before you leave, to check your heart rhythm.
Well, how long does an ECG take?
Ten minutes at most. So, a scan today and an ECG now. Does that make sense?
Fine. Ring my wife if you need me, she'll be furious if I put it off. I'll call my office and move the meeting.
Good decision. The nurse is just next door, and she'll take you through for the ECG now.

negative_findings.finding: weakness in an arm or leg

physical_examination.finding: face moves evenly on both sides

clinical_actions.description: Arrange CT scan of head today
